messages.content: Classify only the semantic relationship in each numbered event. Ignore administrative words such as correction, replacing, update, superseding, source, authority, note, and observation. Return exactly one letter on its own line per input event, preserving order: D means an entity relies on or has an upstream requirement/supporting entity; R means an entity was renamed or redesignated; T means a failure, safety, or minimum-temperature threshold. Examples: 'Correcting an old note, entity a actually relies on entity b' -> D. 'An update superseding an old note says entity a has entity b upstream' -> D. 'Entity a is now called entity b' -> R. 'Entity a fails below 4 C' -> T. No numbering, punctuation, or explanation.

1. [Record r_ca87c09bfdc6cdc2; source UNVERIFIED; event 15] At event time 15, During a routine archive review, the ledger states: For entity d_8dda288d68f073f8, staff now use the name entity d_5a5c140d26dc7fe5. This was recorded alongside unrelated scheduling notes.
2. [Record r_30b64165b0f64e0d; source CURATED; event 16] At event time 16, During a routine archive review, the ledger states: Regarding entity d_bca55b91b989108c, its upstream requirement is entity d_270005fdaa946cf9. No other part of the archival narrative changed this statement.
3. [Record r_ba56c62dbcbae8ea; source UNVERIFIED; event 17] At event time 17, In the ordinary course of plant reporting, the ledger states: Entity d_230f73028793a51a cannot proceed without entity d_e581ab86074b58a8. The filing also mentioned routine paperwork with no operational consequence.
